item.title: Overflow and Carry
item.description: I’ve been working on uplifting PIC Mid-Range device assemblies to Rizin’s RzIL. This has been quite interesting work so far but I encountered a conceptual blockage just when I started uplifting arithmetic instructions. I won’t talk much about my work in Rizin here but you can seach around the blog to find related posts. I want this post to be as short as possible for those who just want the concept and not my story!

item.title: Writing Pic Uplifters
item.description: In last post we went through the general reference manual. Turns out (after going through some datasheets), it’s better to divide the whole IL uplifting process into families like : PIC16FXXXX PIC18FXXXX PIC32FXXXX (completely different device!, take a look) etc… Why? Well because I went through the datasheets and it looks like the reference manual we referred to is outdated and new devices were added to family with more memory banks!

item.title: Rzil PIC Uplifting
item.description: I’ve already explained the working of RzIL in this post. If you are a beginner or someone who is reading this blog just to explore a new topc, I strongly recommend you to go through that post. Also, if you are a maintainer and find some conceptual mistakes in the posts, please message me ツ about it. So, now I’m assuming you already know how the lifting works on a basic level and also have a basic idea of RzIL.

item.title: RzIL Introductory Notes
item.description: References First Some idea about how RzIL works can be found here : https://github.com/rizinorg/rizin/blob/dev/doc/rzil.md RzIL is based on BAP’s Core Theory so do read about that too. Analysis code is present in librz/include/rz_analysis.h and librz/analysis. ESIL uplifters are present in librz/analysis/p and the new RzIL uplifters are present in librz/analysis/arch. Each of these intermediate languages can be emulated so there must be a VM to interpret these ILs and run them.
